sentences.text: Researchers investigated how hunger influences the avoidance of painful stimuli in fruit flies to allow them to seek food.
In a test where flies had to cross an electric shock barrier to get food, starving the flies made them more tolerant of the shock only if food smells were present.
A specific neural pathway was identified where hunger-sensing cells send signals to other neurons that combine this state with food smells to inhibit shock-reactive neurons.
The activity of shock-reactive neurons was reduced in starved flies when they were exposed to food cues.
The results reveal a brain circuit that uses motivational state to control how aversive signals are processed, steering behavior toward goals.
